blockers.summary: The reviewer (juliank) says the problem has not been reproduced or understood from the boot side, and asks for it to be diagnosed before the patch can be judged. The original hanging-mount bug was reportedly resolved separately with mount namespaces, so the premise for removing the fuseblk fallback is in doubt.

The regression-potential section is factually wrong. os-prober is automatically enabled at install time when other OSes are detected, so it is not simply disabled by default. The section also does not analyse what the fuseblk fallback does, such as which real filesystems (NTFS, exFAT, etc.) now go undetected, before removing it.

The SRU only covers Resolute. The text says the original fix was never backported to Noble and Jammy, and that the newer os-prober should be backported there after this SRU. That leaves the target series and the dependent bug 1987679 changes unclear.

The test plan only shows the snapshot case failing and says the entry will not be added afterwards. It has no explicit verification steps for the fixed package. It also does not check that legitimate filesystems such as NTFS or other-OS partitions are still detected, or that the hanging-mount problem does not return.

comments.author: dgadomski
comments.body: Thanks Arif, I've uploaded it.

blockers.summary: The upload to jammy-proposed was rejected from the queue as 'languishing for over a month', so the fix is not currently in the pipeline and must be re-uploaded.

A behavior change is unaddressed: rados_connect_timeout=0 used to mean 'use the default' but now means 'no timeout', and only values below 0 fall back to the Ceph config. Deployments such as the glance charm that set 0 could hang indefinitely. The SRU template's regression section doesn't cover this.

The test plan is confusing and inconsistent. It is unclear which backends are created and which is disabled ('cinder' is disabled, but the backends are ceph and swift/rgw). It does not state the expected failover behavior or include concrete commands, and a reviewer asked for it to be rewritten.

The [Impact] section is unclear about what the fix does and why it matters, and a reviewer asked for it to be improved. It also doesn't mention that the upstream fix changes the semantics of the option.

The upstream fix is split across two commits: the deprecation and a later change that restores the option. The bug was closed by the deprecation commit, so it is unclear which patches the SRU actually includes. The release-note change and semantic shift are also not reflected in the SRU description.

The verification evidence is only autopkgtest results from a PPA, which don't exercise the timeout failover scenario. The comment mentions an end-user test package, with no detail. The test plan has no recorded verification of the actual behavior, and the PPA version (ppa2) may not match the rejected upload.

There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

comments.author: hemanth-n
comments.body:
CI failure analysis (ubuntu-build for devel):

The CI pipeline builds every branch against the devel series, so this 28.0.0 source was built with devel (tenacious) build-dependencies. Result: 18142 tests, 1962 failures:

- 1959 of them are cinder.tests.unit.policies.* RBAC tests failing in setUp with oslo_config.cfg.NoSuchOptError: no such option enforce_scope in group [oslo_policy] — tenacious ships a newer python3-oslo.policy that removed the legacy enforce_scope option which cinder 28.0.0's policy test base still sets.
- 1 is the posix backup driver environment flake seen on other branches too.
- 0 infinidat test failures — the code changed by this MR passes everywhere it ran.

The same source built for the correct series (2:28.0.0-0ubuntu1.2~ppa1, resolute, in ppa:hemanth-n/openstack-sru-packages) runs the identical suite fully green:
https://launchpad.net/~hemanth-n/+archive/ubuntu/openstack-sru-packages/+build/33987683/+files/buildlog_ubuntu-resolute-amd64.cinder_2%3A28.0.0-0ubuntu1.2~ppa1_BUILDING.txt.gz

The red CI is a pre-existing property of the repo pipeline (wrong-series build for non-devel branches), not introduced by this MR.

comments.author: hemanth-n
comments.body:
CI failure analysis (ubuntu-build for devel):

The full unit suite ran during the CI build: 19069 tests, exactly 1 failure:
cinder.tests.unit.backup.drivers.test_backup_posix.PosixBackupDriverTestCase.test_put_container_disabled
(put_container returned None instead of raising the expected OSError — filesystem-behavior difference in the LP CI LXD build environment).

This failure is unrelated to this change: the patch touches only cinder/volume/drivers/infinidat.py and its unit test file; all infinidat tests pass in CI. The same content built for the correct series in ppa:hemanth-n/openstack-sru-packages runs the identical suite green (see the ~ppa1 test build).
